name: Server-side file read/write from SQL
attack_scenario: Via an injectable query the attacker uses INTO OUTFILE to write a PHP web shell under the web root, then browses to it for full RCE; or uses LOAD_FILE to exfiltrate server secrets.
negative_test_hint: issue the query "SELECT load_file('/etc/passwd')" and assert the database layer rejects it rather than returning server file contents

exemplar.noncompliant: SELECT payload FROM logs INTO OUTFILE '/var/www/html/shell.php';
exemplar.compliant: SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE active = 1;
exemplar.explanation: LOAD_FILE reads arbitrary files readable by the DB service (e.g. /etc/passwd, key material) and INTO OUTFILE/DUMPFILE writes attacker-controlled bytes to any path the service can write. These are the classic MySQL primitives for local file disclosure and web-shell drop (CWE-73/CWE-538); they should never appear in application scripts.
